assumptions: The exertion phase is the upward drive: hip and knee extension with ankle plantarflexion, then overhead shoulder flexion and elbow extension to release the ball.
Both feet stay in contact with the floor during the drive, so the lower body is treated as closed chain.
Both limbs work symmetrically and the load is held in both hands.
Trunk flexion or extension is omitted because the throw's trunk path is not clearly shown, and the trunk is modeled as bracing against extension.
Ankle plantarflexion and scapular upward rotation are accompanying motions and are marked as assist.
The catch and rebound portion is not modeled separately.
classification_reasons: The exercise is a bilateral standing two-handed medicine ball overhead throw, which fits the jump_and_throw family and the joint-action vocabulary.
The contact sheet shows a lowered hip and knee flexed loading position with the ball near the knees, then a tall extended finish with the ball overhead behind the head.

The instructions and images differ slightly on the start, since the text starts with the ball behind the head and the frames show a lower countermovement. They agree on the exertion phase: lower-body drive, then overhead arm extension and release.

instructions: Begin standing while facing a wall or a partner.
Using both hands, position the ball behind your head, stretching as much as possible, and forcefully throw the ball forward.

Ensure that you follow your throw through, being prepared to receive your rebound from your throw. If you are throwing against the wall, make sure that you stand close enough to the wall to receive the rebound, and aim a little higher than you would with a partner.
